ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the input loop labeled input loop, and the input current is labeled i1. Above the input terminal, it first passes through a 1 kΩ resistor, then passes through a vertical 1 kΩ resistor to reach the middle node. This middle node is connected downward to a 100 µF capacitor to the bottom reference line. To the right of the middle node is connected a controlled current source, with the arrow inside the source pointing downward, labeled 49i1, indicating that this controlled source injects current proportional to i1 into the middle node. On the right side, a 1 kΩ resistor and a 100 µF capacitor branch can also be seen. Reasoning: Write KCL at the middle capacitor node; the current flowing into this node and entering the middle 100 µF capacitor is the sum of the input current and the controlled-source current: i_C = i1 + 49i1 = 50i1. For the middle capacitor, i_C = s(100 µF)v. Therefore s(100 µF)v = 50i1, so v/i1 = 50/[s(100 µF)]. Writing it in the equivalent capacitance form 1/(sC_eq), obtain C_eq = 100 µF/50 = 2 µF.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the left input loop current i1, the two series 1 kΩ resistors leading to the central node, the central 100 µF capacitor to the bottom reference, and the downward dependent current source 49i1 feeding that central node. Then write KCL at the central capacitive node: the capacitor current is the sum of the input current and the dependent-source current, so i_C = i1 + 49i1 = 50i1. With i_C = s(100 µF)v, solve v/i1 = 50/[s(100 µF)]. Match this to 1/(sC_eq), yielding C_eq = 100 µF/50 = 2 µF.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is a direct node-current method: it uses the controlled current source to find the effective current charging the input-loop capacitor, rather than reducing the whole circuit by series/parallel capacitor rules.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit topology from the image: the input current is labeled i1 at the left; it passes through two 1 kΩ resistors before reaching the central node. A 100 µF capacitor connects this central node to the bottom reference line. A dependent current source labeled 49i1, with arrow downward, injects current into the same central node from the right-hand branch. Another 100 µF capacitor is on the far right branch, but the key input-loop capacitive node is the central one.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text prompt only to know the requested quantity: the equivalent capacitance seen by the input loop of the shown circuit.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use capacitor relation in the s-domain, i_C = s C v. The two left 1 kΩ resistors only add resistive voltage drops and do not change the equivalent capacitance. The dependent current source contributes an additional 49i1 into the central capacitor node, so the central 100 µF capacitor is charged by total current i1 + 49i1 = 50i1. Therefore v/i1 = 50/(s·100 µF) = 1/(s·2 µF), giving C_eq = 2 µF.
